title: "It's all in your mind": attitudes and why people act as they do
summary: Bunn muses that whatever people do is in their minds, including why people want to hit others or why interviewer and interviewee are together.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Yeah. It's all in your mind, to tell you the truth, Chuck.

It's all in your mind. Whatever you're doing, it's in your mind. Now, I go out there, go out in the street somewhere, and somebody comes running along and hits me with something, you know what I mean?
It's all in their mind. Why do they want to hit me? [Because I'm standing out there,] in the street. But just like me, I wouldn't go out there and hit nobody.
But yet and still, whatever I hear or see or play, I mean it's all in my mind. In the first place, I don't go out to bother nobody.
Why do that? That's getting yourself in
Why do you think some -- you're talking about the inclination of the mind.
The way it turns, or what direction.
Why do you think certain people tend to go one direction and some people in another?
It's because they've got their mind to do it.
It's in their mind, why. That's what a lot of them want to know, why. Why are you here? Why am I sitting down here talking to you? You see?
It's things like that. And in my mind you come here to help me and I come here to help you.
No jealousy or nothing amounting to it.
It's just something you want to do. If I didn't want to do it, I wouldn't be in here. And if you didn't want to do it, you wouldn't be here.

Okay. That's it. Anything you want to do you're going to do, regardless. Nobody can keep you from it. It's like someone says, 'Well, I'm going up to Teddy Bunn's house tonight and see what he -- if he can go out. And if he can't go out, I'm going to hit him in his mouth.' You understand? Some people are like that. You know?
